name: Rostral pons
summary: The upper pons is the level of the trigeminal nerve: its motor and principal sensory nuclei sit in the lateral tegmentum and the root leaves the lateral surface between the basis and the middle cerebellar peduncle. The basis pontis is at its widest, the superior cerebellar peduncles form the lateral walls of the narrowing fourth ventricle, and the lateral lemniscus carries auditory fibers up toward the inferior colliculus. The locus coeruleus lies in the floor of the ventricle near the upper end of this level.

anatomy.location: From the trigeminal root entry zone up to the isthmus where the pons meets the midbrain; MNI z ≈ −24 to −32.

subdivisions.name: Basis pontis
subdivisions.note: corticospinal, corticobulbar and corticopontine fibers among the pontine nuclei; transverse fibers to the middle cerebellar peduncle

subdivisions.name: Trigeminal motor nucleus
subdivisions.note: medial to the principal sensory nucleus; motor root to the muscles of mastication

subdivisions.name: Principal (chief) sensory nucleus of V
subdivisions.note: discriminative touch from the face; lateral tegmentum at the root entry

subdivisions.name: Mesencephalic nucleus of V
subdivisions.note: proprioception from the jaw muscles; extends into the midbrain

subdivisions.name: Medial lemniscus, trigeminal lemniscus and spinothalamic tract
subdivisions.note: a horizontal band of ascending sensory fibers across the ventral tegmentum

subdivisions.name: Lateral lemniscus
subdivisions.note: ascending auditory fibers on the lateral edge of the tegmentum

subdivisions.name: Superior cerebellar peduncle
subdivisions.note: dorsolateral, forming the wall of the fourth ventricle, carrying dentate outflow toward the red nucleus and thalamus

subdivisions.name: Locus coeruleus
subdivisions.note: pigmented noradrenergic nucleus in the lateral floor of the upper fourth ventricle

subdivisions.name: Pontine reticular formation
subdivisions.note: central tegmentum; arousal and motor modulation

function: Relays facial touch and controls chewing through the trigeminal system, carries the auditory pathway toward the midbrain, transmits cerebellar outflow in the superior peduncle, and houses part of the ascending reticular activating system.

bestView.label: mid-to-upper pons at the trigeminal root entry
trigeminal root leaving the lateral pons
superior cerebellar peduncles flanking the upper fourth ventricle

imaging.normalAppearance: On axial T2 the trigeminal roots are seen as paired oblique dark bands crossing the prepontine cistern from the lateral pons toward Meckel's cave; the superior cerebellar peduncles border the ventricle posterolaterally.

pathology.finding: T2/FLAIR-bright plaque at the root entry zone (multiple sclerosis) or neurovascular contact with the SCA on high-resolution T2, presenting as trigeminal neuralgia or facial numbness.
Wedge of restricted diffusion in the upper basis pontis; ataxic hemiparesis or dysarthria–clumsy hand.
Diffuse expansion of the pons with T2 hyperintensity engulfing the basilar artery, mostly in children.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Thin axial T2/FLAIR and DWI; CISS/FIESTA for the trigeminal root

lesionEffects.deficit: Ipsilateral facial numbness and weak jaw deviating toward the lesion
lesionEffects.mechanism: Principal sensory and motor trigeminal nuclei or the root
Corticospinal fibers in the basis pontis

lesionEffects.deficit: Contralateral loss of all sensory modalities on the body
lesionEffects.mechanism: Medial lemniscus and spinothalamic tract lying together in the tegmentum
Superior cerebellar peduncle before its decussation, or pontocerebellar fibers
Descending sympathetic fibers in the lateral tegmentum

examination: Corneal reflex, facial light touch and pin-prick in all three divisions
pearls: Trigeminal signs with contralateral hemiparesis or hemisensory loss localize to the rostral pons
At this level the two sensory systems lie side by side, so a single lesion can abolish all modalities on the contralateral body while the ipsilateral face is affected
